questions.title: Hypotenuse With Math Import
questions.description:
Your geometry app needs roof-slope lengths. Import the standard-library math module and use math.hypot to compute the hypotenuse of a right triangle from its two perpendicular side lengths.

Input Format:
One line with two floats a and b separated by a space (the two legs).

Output Format:
Print math.hypot(a, b) formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import math

a, b = map(float, input().split())
print(f"{math.hypot(a, b):.2f}")

questions.title: Greatest Common Divisor Drill
questions.description:
Practice calling into an imported module. Read two integers and print their greatest common divisor using math.gcd from the math module.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b separated by a space.

Output Format:
Print math.gcd(a, b).

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 1000000 and a + b > 0
questions.sourcecode:
import math

a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(math.gcd(a, b))

questions.title: Factorial From Math Module
questions.description:
A quiz generator needs factorials. Import the math module and print math.factorial(n) for the given n. Note that math.factorial(0) returns 1.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
Print math.factorial(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 15
questions.sourcecode:
import math

n = int(input())
print(math.factorial(n))

questions.title: Seeded Coin Flip Sequence
questions.description:
A board-game simulator needs reproducible coin tosses, so it seeds Python's random module with a fixed seed before flipping. Read a seed and a count, call random.seed(seed), then generate k values with random.randint(1, 2) (1 means heads, 2 means tails).

Input Format:
One line with two integers: seed and k.

Output Format:
Print k letters H or T (one per flip) separated by single spaces, in generation order.

Constraints:
0 <= seed <= 10000, 1 <= k <= 50
questions.sampleoutput1: T H T H H H T H
questions.output1: T T H T T T
questions.output2: H H T H T T T
questions.output3: T H T H T T H T T
questions.sourcecode:
import random

seed, k = map(int, input().split())
random.seed(seed)
flips = []
for _ in range(k):
    r = random.randint(1, 2)
    flips.append("H" if r == 1 else "T")
print(" ".join(flips))

questions.title: Circle Area With Math Pi
questions.description:
A laser-cutter planner estimates disc areas. Import math and compute the area of a circle of radius r using math.pi, printing the result with 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with the float r.

Output Format:
Print math.pi * r * r formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 <= r <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import math

r = float(input())
print(f"{math.pi * r * r:.2f}")

questions.title: Main Guard Greeter Drill
questions.description:
Emulate a tiny greeting module. Define a function greet(name) that returns the text Hello, <name>! and place the actual work under the standard if __name__ == "__main__": guard so the file behaves like a proper script. The name arrives on stdin.

Input Format:
One line with the name (no spaces).

Output Format:
Print greet(name) exactly, e.g. Hello, Ada!

Constraints:
1 <= len(name) <= 50, name has no spaces

questions.title: Sensor Batch Mean Check
questions.description:
A greenhouse controller batches temperature readings and asks the statistics module for the batch mean. Read n and then n values, and report statistics.mean of the batch.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated floats.

Output Format:
Print the mean formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
import statistics

n = int(input())
values = [float(x) for x in input().split()]
print(f"{statistics.mean(values):.2f}")

questions.title: Friday The Thirteenth Finder
questions.description:
An event planner avoids scheduling launches on spooky dates. Using the calendar module, decide whether the given month contains a Friday the 13th. calendar.weekday(year, month, day) returns 0 for Monday through 6 for Sunday, so Friday is weekday 4.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: year and month.

Output Format:
Print Yes if the 13th of that month falls on a Friday, otherwise print No.

Constraints:
2000 <= year <= 2100, 1 <= month <= 12
questions.sourcecode:
import calendar

year, month = map(int, input().split())
weekday = calendar.weekday(year, month, 13)
print("Yes" if weekday == 4 else "No")

questions.title: Asset Path Assembler
questions.description:
A game build pipeline stores every asset under a base folder. Assemble the full asset location with os.path.join instead of gluing strings together by hand: read a base folder, a subfolder and a filename on three lines, and print the joined path.

Input Format:
Line 1: base folder.
Line 2: subfolder.
Line 3: filename.

Output Format:
Print os.path.join(base, subfolder, filename).

Constraints:
each line has length 1 to 60 and contains no leading slash
questions.sourcecode:
import os

base = input()
folder = input()
filename = input()
print(os.path.join(base, folder, filename))

questions.title: Median Clinic Wait Report
questions.description:
A clinic reviews yesterday's waiting times and wants the median, which is less skewed by one extreme patient. Read n and the n waiting times, and report statistics.median of the list.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers (minutes).

Output Format:
Print the median formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= minute <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
import statistics

n = int(input())
minutes = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
print(f"{statistics.median(minutes):.2f}")

questions.title: Lucky Draw Session Audit
questions.description:
Your game studio runs a deterministic lucky-draw simulator to balance loot tables. It seeds Python's random module with a fixed seed, draws k integers in the range 1..100 with random.randint, then audits the session.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: seed k threshold.

Output Format:
Line 1: the k drawn numbers in generation order, space separated.
Line 2: how many draws were greater than or equal to threshold.
Line 3: the highest drawn number.
Line 4: how many distinct values were drawn.

Constraints:
0 <= seed <= 10000, 3 <= k <= 60, 1 <= threshold <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
import random

seed, k, threshold = map(int, input().split())
random.seed(seed)
draws = []
for _ in range(k):
    draws.append(random.randint(1, 100))

top = draws[0]
jackpots = 0
for d in draws:
    if d > top:
        top = d
    if d >= threshold:
        jackpots += 1

distinct = []
for d in draws:
    if d not in distinct:
        distinct.append(d)

print(" ".join(str(d) for d in draws))
print(jackpots)
print(top)
print(len(distinct))

questions.title: Statistics Bureau Report
questions.description:
The city statistics bureau summarizes survey batches. Use the statistics module (not hand-written formulas) to report the mean, median and sample standard deviation of a batch of measurements.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated floats.

Output Format:
Line 1: statistics.mean formatted to 2 decimal places.
Line 2: statistics.median formatted to 2 decimal places.
Line 3: statistics.stdev formatted to 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 100, 0 <= value <= 100000
questions.sourcecode:
import statistics

n = int(input())
values = [float(x) for x in input().split()]
print(f"{statistics.mean(values):.2f}")
print(f"{statistics.median(values):.2f}")
print(f"{statistics.stdev(values):.2f}")

questions.title: Guarded Converter Command Deck
questions.description:
A weather dashboard ships a temperature module. Emulate it in a single file: define the conversion functions celsius_to_fahrenheit, fahrenheit_to_celsius and celsius_to_kelvin at module level, register them in a dict, and run the whole command handling under if __name__ == "__main__": so importing the file would only expose the functions.

Input Format:
Line 1: the command, one of c2f, f2c, c2k.
Line 2: the value as a float.

Output Format:
Print the converted value formatted to exactly 2 decimal places. c2f: c*9/5+32; f2c: (f-32)*5/9; c2k: c+273.15.

Constraints:
command is one of c2f, f2c, c2k; -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Splitext Asset Probe
questions.description:
An asset pipeline reads path fragments and inspects the assembled file. Assemble the path with os.path.join from the given parts, then report the file name (os.path.basename) and its extension (os.path.splitext, printed without the leading dot, or none when there is no extension).

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n (number of path parts).
Lines 2..n+1: one path part per line, in order.

Output Format:
Line 1: the full joined path.
Line 2: the base name of the file.
Line 3: the extension without a dot, or none.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5, each part has length 1 to 40
questions.sourcecode:
import os

n = int(input())
parts = [input() for _ in range(n)]
full = os.path.join(*parts)
print(full)
print(os.path.basename(full))
ext = os.path.splitext(full)[1]
print(ext[1:] if ext else "none")

questions.title: Monthrange First Day Report
questions.description:
A scheduling tool needs each month's length and the weekday of its first day. Use calendar.monthrange(year, month) for the number of days and calendar.weekday(year, month, 1) for the first day (0 is Monday). No datetime objects allowed in this drill.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: year and month.

Output Format:
Line 1: the number of days in the month.
Line 2: the English weekday name of the 1st: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday.

Constraints:
2000 <= year <= 2100, 1 <= month <= 12
questions.sourcecode:
import calendar

year, month = map(int, input().split())
days = calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]
names = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
first = calendar.weekday(year, month, 1)
print(days)
print(names[first])

questions.title: Stdin Log Line Digest
questions.description:
A build tool swallows an entire pasted build log from standard input before producing one digest. Read every line with sys.stdin (do not use input()), then report the number of log entries, the total number of characters excluding newlines, and the length of the longest line.

Input Format:
One or more lines of log text on stdin.

Output Format:
Line 1: number of lines.
Line 2: total characters across all lines, excluding newline characters.
Line 3: length of the longest line.

Constraints:
1 <= lines <= 50, each line has length 1 to 80
questions.sourcecode:
import sys

lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
total = 0
longest = 0
for line in lines:
    total += len(line)
    if len(line) > longest:
        longest = len(line)
print(len(lines))
print(total)
print(longest)

questions.title: Seeded Dice Streak Ledger
questions.description:
A casino hardware lab stress-tests dice with a deterministic thrower. Seed Python's random module with the given seed, roll a six-sided die k times using random.randint(1, 6), then produce a full audit of the session.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: seed and k.

Output Format:
Line 1: six counts space separated, one per face from 1 to 6.
Line 2: the length of the longest run of identical consecutive rolls.
Line 3: the most frequent face; if several faces tie, print the smallest face.
Line 4: how many adjacent pairs of rolls were equal.

Constraints:
0 <= seed <= 10000, 5 <= k <= 500

questions.title: Geometry Toolbox Suite
questions.description:
A CAD plug-in exposes a geometry toolbox of module-level functions. Implement circle_area(r) as math.pi * r * r, triangle_area(a, b, c) with Heron's formula via math.sqrt, and distance(x1, y1, x2, y2) with math.hypot, then process the incoming commands under an if __name__ == "__main__": guard. A triangle whose sides are non-positive or violate the triangle inequality must report Invalid triangle instead of a number.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n (number of commands).
Lines 2..n+1: one command per line, either circle r, tri a b c or dist x1 y1 x2 y2 (all numbers are floats).

Output Format:
One line per command, in order: the result formatted to exactly 2 decimal places, or the exact text Invalid triangle.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20; 0 <= r <= 100; 0 <= side <= 100; -100 <= coordinate <= 100

questions.title: Guarded Text Toolkit CLI
questions.description:
A text-processing package is emulated in one file. Define the functions shout (upper case), whisper (lower case), mirror (reverse the text) and repeat (text repeated k times) at module level, wire them into a command table, and run the command loop under if __name__ == "__main__":. Commands arrive as lines; a command word not in the table prints Unknown command. Only shout, whisper and mirror take the remainder of the line as their text; repeat takes a word and an integer count separated by a space.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n (number of commands).
Lines 2..n+1: one command per line, e.g. shout hello world or repeat ab 3.

Output Format:
One line per command with its result, or Unknown command. After all commands print ok X bad Y where X counts successful commands and Y counts unknown ones.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20; text length 1 to 60; repeat count 0 <= k <= 9

shout hello world
mirror racecar
repeat ab 3
jump x
questions.sampleoutput1:
HELLO WORLD
racecar
ababab
Unknown command
ok 3 bad 1
questions.input1:
3
whisper AAA BBB
mirror a
repeat x 0
questions.input2:
3
repeat ab 2
mirror level
shout Py ThOn
questions.output2:
abab
level
PY THON
ok 3 bad 0

questions.title: Asset Pipeline Manifest Audit
questions.description:
A release pipeline audits its manifest. Read the base folder and then n asset names. For each asset, join it onto the base with os.path.join and classify it by extension using os.path.splitext: extensions py, js, ts are code; json, csv, yaml, xml are data; md, txt are doc; anything else (or no extension) is other. The extension is printed without its leading dot, or as none. Note that splitext treats a leading dot (as in .hidden) as part of the name, so such files have no extension. A name may itself contain slashes (e.g. img/logo.png) - basename still applies to the final path.

Input Format:
Line 1: the base folder.
Line 2: the integer n.
Lines 3..n+2: one asset name per line.

Output Format:
One line per asset: basename extension class (e.g. app.py py code). Then a summary line: code a data b doc c other d with the four class counts.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20; base and names have length 1 to 40
questions.sampleoutput1:
app.py py code
notes.md md doc
readme none other
code 1 data 0 doc 1 other 1
questions.sampleoutput2:
.hidden none other
blob none other
code 0 data 0 doc 0 other 2
questions.output1:
archive.tar.gz gz other
code 0 data 0 doc 0 other 1
questions.output2:
run.js js code
data.json json data
schema.yaml yaml data
song.mp3 mp3 other
code 1 data 2 doc 0 other 1
questions.output3:
notes.md md doc
logo.png png other
main.ts ts code
code 1 data 0 doc 1 other 1
